mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS signals monetary easing that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as long as the trend persists.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in < 40% of periods with declining FEDFUNDS, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0% for three consecutive months, it indicates labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in CPIAUCSL (inflation) and FEDFUNDS (interest rates) signal aggressive monetary tightening that compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer confidence and construction activity that drives positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of late-cycle expansion periods when HOUST is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) reflects robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in < 40% of periods with rising PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 for two consecutive months, it indicates weakening manufacturing output and economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100 for two months.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) declines while inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises, it signals stagflationary pressures that compress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 < 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, rising FEDFUNDS rates increase the cost of capital and reduce equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is rising.
